chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and enters into her (consummates the marriage) before giving her anything. He said: 'It is a debt upon him.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband consummates marriage before paying the dowry?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that consummating marriage prior to paying the dowry does not invalidate the union but converts the unpaid portion into a binding debt (*dayn*) on the husband. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the dowry is an immediate financial right of the wife, enforceable even before its formal stipulation or payment, thereby protecting her economic security within the marital contract.
